common_subject_case.interpretation: A valid existence-dependent common-subject case absent from the nine displayed formulas under either explicit matching convention. Historical 'form' equivalence may be broader; no claim to have reconstructed it.

A5_empty_A_counterexample.name: A5 fails with A empty even when B and C are nonempty

I_does_not_imply_O.name: One shared witness, no witness in A minus B

common_subject_empty_A_counterexample.name: A(A,B) and A(A,C) do not ensure I(C,B) when A is empty

pear_tree_equality_counterexample.name: A=trees, B=pear trees; inclusion and some pears allow equality

pear_tree_strict_inclusion_example.name: A=trees, B=pear trees; the extra non-pear tree supplies strictness

model_space.completeness_basis: The region-abstraction theorem in PROOF.md, not a bounded numeric extrapolation.
model_space.occupancy_bit_meaning: bit r records occupancy of type r, whose bits record membership in A,B,C
model_space.zero_mask_policy: Add one outside-all-terms witness; raw 0 and raw 1 are equivalent.

scope: Modern set-theoretic reconstruction of nine supplied CIII forms; not a claim about all of Euler's syllogistic.

semantics.A(X,Y): X is a subset of Y (no existential import)
semantics.E(X,Y): X and Y are disjoint (no existential import)
semantics.I(X,Y): X and Y have a nonempty intersection
